\begin{enumerate}
    \item When $\rho=0$, there is no difference between iid estimation $(\hat{\mathbf{A}}^\dagger(t), \hat{\bb}^\dagger)$ and paired estimation $(\hat{\mathbf{A}}^*(t), \hat{\bb}^*)$.
    \item The larger the $\rho$ is, the better the paired estimation $\hat{\mathbf{A}}^*(t)$ is than iid $\hat{\mathbf{A}}^\dagger(t)$.
    \item The larger the $\rho$ is, the harder to estimate $\bb$ for both paired estimation $\hat{\bb}^*$ and iid estimation $\hat{\bb}^*$.
    \item All estimation errors decrease as $n$ increases.
\end{enumerate}
